title.zh: 卷二百五十九 列傳第十八 張美 郭守文 尹崇珂 劉廷讓 袁繼忠 崔彥進 張廷翰 皇甫繼明 張瓊
title.en: Volume 259 Biographies 18: Zhang Mei, Guo Shuowen, Yin Chongke, Liu Tingrang, Yuan Jizhong, Cui Yanjin, Zhang Tinghan, Huangfu Jiming, Zhangg Qiong
title.raw: 卷二百五十九 列傳第十八 張美 郭守文 尹崇珂 劉廷讓 袁繼忠 崔彥進 張廷翰 皇甫繼明 張瓊 Volume 259 Biographies 18: Zhang Mei, Guo Shuowen, Yin Chongke, Liu Tingrang, Yuan Jizhong, Cui Yanjin, Zhang Tinghan, Huangfu Jiming, Zhangg Qiong

sentences.zh: 張美，字玄珪，貝州清河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, styled Xuangui, was a man of Qinghe in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, styled Xuangui, was a native of Qinghe in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 少善書計，初為左藏小吏，以彊幹聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in writing and reckoning; he first served as a minor clerk in the Left Treasury and became known for forceful competence.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at writing and accounts; he began as a junior clerk in the Left Treasury and won a reputation for forceful efficiency.

sentences.zh: 三司薦奏，特補本庫專知，出為澶州糧料使。

translations.literal: The Three Offices recommended him in memorial; he was specially appointed specialist in charge of that repository and went out as Grain Commissary of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices recommended him to the throne, and he was specially appointed specialist in charge of that depot; he was then posted as grain commissary of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 周世宗鎮澶淵，每有求取，美必曲為供給。

translations.literal: When Shizong of Zhou was stationed at Chanyuan, whenever he made demands Mei would bend rules to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizong of Zhou was garrisoned at Chanyuan, whenever he asked for supplies Mei would bend the rules to furnish them.

sentences.zh: 周祖聞之怒，將譴責之，而恐傷世宗意，徙美為濮州馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder heard of this and grew angry, intending to reprimand him, but fearing to wound Shizong's feelings, he transferred Mei to be Deputy Commander of Horse and Foot Armies at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder heard of it and was furious, intending to punish him, but fearing to offend Shizong he instead transferred Mei to be deputy commander of the horse-and-foot armies at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，世宗再幸淮上，皆為大內都點檢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Shizong again visited the Huai region, [Mei] each time served as Chief Inspector of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Shizong again toured the Huai region, Mei served both times as chief inspector of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 北征，又為大內都部署。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign he again served as Chief Deployer of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition he again served as chief deployer of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 師還，為左監門衛上將軍，充宣徽北院使，判三司。

translations.literal: When the army returned he became General-in-Chief of the Left Directorate of Gate Guards, concurrently Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate, and Acting Director of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was made general-in-chief of the Left Directorate of Gate Guards, appointed commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Directorate, and given charge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 美彊力有心計，周知其利病，每有所條奏釐革，上多可之，常以幹敏稱。

translations.literal: Mei was forceful and resourceful, thoroughly knowing what was profitable and harmful; whenever he submitted proposals for reform the ruler mostly approved them, and he was constantly praised for competence and alertness.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was forceful and shrewd, with a thorough grasp of what worked and what did not; his memorials proposing reforms were usually approved, and he was widely praised for competence and quick judgment.

sentences.zh: 世宗連歲征討，糧饋不乏，深委賴焉。

translations.literal: Shizong campaigned year after year, yet grain supplies never ran short, and he relied on Mei deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong campaigned year after year without ever lacking provisions, and he came to rely on Mei heavily.

sentences.zh: 然以澶淵有所求假，頗薄之，美亦自愧。

translations.literal: Yet because of the favors sought at Chanyuan he somewhat looked down on him, and Mei himself also felt ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of the indulgence Mei had shown at Chanyuan, Shizong thought rather less of him, and Mei himself was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, [Mei] was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor with nominal commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Mei was given the additional title of honorary grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Grand Marshal with nominal commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was given the additional title of honorary grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 初，李筠鎮上黨，募亡命，多為不法，漸倔彊難制。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Yun had garrisoned Shangdang, recruiting fugitives who mostly acted unlawfully, and he gradually grew defiant and hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Yun held Shangdang and recruited fugitives who committed many illegal acts; he grew increasingly defiant and difficult to control.

sentences.zh: 美度筠必叛，陰積粟於懷、孟間。

translations.literal: Mei judged that Yun would surely rebel and secretly stored grain between Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Mei judged that Li Yun would rebel and quietly stockpiled grain in the Huai and Meng region.

sentences.zh: 後筠果叛，太祖親討之，大軍十萬出太行，經費無闕，美有力焉。

translations.literal: Later Yun did rebel; Taizu personally campaigned against him, and when an army of a hundred thousand marched out through Taihang the expenses were never wanting — Mei had a large part in this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun did rebel; Taizu led the campaign in person, and when a hundred-thousand-man force marched out through Taihang Pass supplies never ran short — Mei had done much to make that possible.

sentences.zh: 拜定國軍節度。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 縣官市木關中，同州歲出緡錢數十萬以假民，長吏十取其一，謂之率分錢，歲至數百萬，美獨不取。

translations.literal: When the government bought timber in Guanzhong, Tongzhou each year issued several hundred thousand strings of cash to lend the people; the chief officials took one part in ten, calling it the apportionment fee, which yearly reached several million — Mei alone did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: When the government bought timber in Guanzhong, Tongzhou each year issued several hundred thousand strings of cash to lend the people; local officials took a tenth as their cut, called the apportionment fee, which yearly amounted to millions — Mei alone refused his share.

sentences.zh: 未幾，他郡有詣闕訴長吏受率分錢者，皆命償之。

translations.literal: Before long, in other prefectures there were those who came to court to accuse chief officials of taking apportionment fees, and all were ordered to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Before long people from other prefectures came to court accusing officials of taking apportionment fees, and the court ordered every offender to repay what he had taken.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，移鎮滄州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was transferred to garrison Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was transferred to command at Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初來朝，改左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he came to court and was changed to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he came to court and was made general-in-chief of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 美獻都城西河曲灣果園二、蔬圃六、亭舍六十餘區。

translations.literal: Mei presented two orchards, six vegetable gardens, and more than sixty pavilions and lodges at Hequ Bay west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mei presented to the throne two orchards, six vegetable gardens, and more than sixty pavilions at Hequ Bay west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 八年，請老，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he requested retirement and left office with his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he asked to retire and was allowed to leave office with his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，諡恭惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was given the posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era he was given the posthumous title Gonghui, "Respectful and Kind."

sentences.zh: 子守瑛，至供備庫使。

translations.literal: His son Shouying rose to be Commissioner of the Supply Reserve Depot.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouying rose to be commissioner of the supply reserve depot.

sentences.zh: 孫士宗，至內殿承制。

translations.literal: His grandson Shizong rose to be Inner Palace Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shizong rose to be an inner-palace drafter.

sentences.zh: 士宗卒，士禹為崇班，士安至閤門祗候，士宣為禮賓副使。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, Shiyu became a member of the Honored Class; Shi'an rose to Gate Attendant; Shixuan became Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong died, Shiyu held a honored-class post; Shi'an became a gate attendant; Shixuan became vice commissioner of ceremonial reception.

sentences.zh: 郭守文

translations.literal: Guo Shuowen
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shuowen

sentences.zh: 郭守文，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Guo Shuowen was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shuowen was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父暉，仕漢為護聖軍使，從周祖征河中，戰死。

translations.literal: His father Hui served the Later Han as commissioner of the Guard of Sacred Protection; he followed the Zhou founder on the campaign against Hezhong and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served the Later Han as commissioner of the Guard of Sacred Protection; he followed the Zhou founder on the campaign against Hezhong and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 守文年十四，居喪哀毀，周祖憐之，召隸帳下。

translations.literal: Shuowen was fourteen; in mourning he was so grief-stricken that he wasted away, and the Zhou founder pitied him and summoned him to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shuowen was fourteen; in mourning he grieved so deeply that he was wasting away, and the Zhou founder took pity on him and brought him into his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補左班殿直，再遷東第二班副都知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed Left Class Palace Attendant and was twice promoted to Deputy Chief of the Eastern Second Class.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed a left-class palace attendant and was twice promoted to deputy chief of the eastern second class.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was promoted to Western Head Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was promoted to western-head palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，遷知簡州。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was transferred to administer Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was appointed prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時劍外多寇，守文悉招來集附。

translations.literal: At that time beyond the Sword Pass there were many bandits; Shuowen summoned them all to come and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were numerous beyond the Sword Pass; Shuowen induced them all to submit and settle under his authority.

sentences.zh: 從潘美征嶺南，會擒劉鋹，遣守文馳傳告捷，遷翰林副使。

translations.literal: He followed Pan Mei on the campaign in Lingnan; when Liu Chang was captured he was sent by express relay to report the victory and was promoted to Vice Hanlin Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pan Mei on the Lingnan campaign; when Liu Chang was captured he was sent by express relay to report the victory and was promoted to vice Hanlin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從曹彬等平金陵，護送李煜歸闕下。

translations.literal: He followed Cao Bin and others in pacifying Jinling and escorted Li Yu back to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cao Bin and others in pacifying Jinling and escorted Li Yu to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時煜以拒命頗自歉，不欲生見太祖。

translations.literal: At that time Yu, because he had resisted orders, felt quite ashamed and did not wish to meet Taizu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, ashamed of having resisted the throne, did not wish to face Taizu while still alive.

sentences.zh: 守文察知之，因謂煜曰：「國家止務恢復疆土，以致太平，豈復有後至之責耶？

translations.literal: Shuowen perceived this and therefore said to Yu, "The state only seeks to recover territory and bring peace — how could there still be blame for coming late?
translations.idiomatic: Shuowen noticed this and said to Li Yu, "The court seeks only to recover the realm and secure peace — why should there be any blame for submitting later than others?

sentences.zh: 」煜心遂安。

translations.literal: " Yu's heart was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yu's mind was put at ease.

sentences.zh: 改西京作坊使、領翰林司事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and put in charge of Hanlin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the western-capital workshops and placed in charge of Hanlin affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄從党進破並寇於團柏谷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Dang Jin in defeating the Bingzhou raiders at Tuanbai Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Dang Jin in defeating the Bingzhou raiders at Tuanbai Valley.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，秦州內附，蕃部騷動，命守文乘傳撫諭，西夏悅伏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo Qinzhou submitted; the tribal departments were unsettled, and Shuowen was ordered to travel by relay post to soothe and instruct them; the Western Xia were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo, when Qinzhou submitted and tribal groups grew restless, Shuowen was sent by express post to reassure them; the Western Xia were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to western upper gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是夏，汴水決於寧陵，發宋、亳丁壯四千五百塞之，命守文董其役。

translations.literal: That summer the Bian River burst its banks at Ningling; four thousand five hundred able-bodied men from Song and Bo were mobilized to block it, and Shuowen was ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Bian River broke through at Ningling; four thousand five hundred laborers from Song and Bo were mobilized to seal the breach, and Shuowen was put in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 是冬，又與閤門副使王侁、西八作副使石全振護塞靈河縣決河。

translations.literal: That winter, together with Vice Gate Commissioner Wang Shen and Western Eight Workshops Vice Commissioner Shi Quanzhen, he oversaw blocking the breach of the Yellow River at Linghe County.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he joined Vice Gate Commissioner Wang Shen and Western Workshops Vice Commissioner Shi Quanzhen in sealing the Yellow River breach at Linghe County.

sentences.zh: 及征太原，守文與判四方館事梁迥分護行營馬步軍。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was attacked, Shuowen and Liang Jiong, who handled affairs of the Four Directions Bureau, jointly protected the campaign army's horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Taiyuan, Shuowen and Liang Jiong of the Four Directions Bureau jointly commanded the escort of the campaign army's horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 會劉繼元降，其弟繼文據代州，依遼人之援以拒命，遣守文討平之。

translations.literal: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, his younger brother Jiwen held Daizhou, relying on Liao aid to resist orders; Shuowen was sent to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, his brother Jiwen held Daizhou and, with Liao support, refused to submit; Shuowen was sent to suppress him and restore order.

sentences.zh: 俄受詔護定州屯兵，大破遼人於蒲城。

translations.literal: Soon he received orders to escort the garrison troops at Dingzhou and inflicted a great defeat on the Liao at Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to escort the garrison at Dingzhou and routed the Liao forces at Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 以功遷東上閤門使、領澶州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and given charge of Cangzhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to eastern upper gate commissioner and appointed prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，擢拜內客省使。

translations.literal: He was recalled and elevated to Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and promoted to commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.

sentences.zh: 八年，滑州房村河決，發卒塞之，命守文董其役。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Fangcun River at Huazhou burst; troops were mobilized to block it, and Shuowen was ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Fangcun River at Huazhou broke its banks; troops were mobilized to seal the breach, and Shuowen was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 遼人擾雄州，命守文率禁兵數萬人赴援，既至，遼人遁去。

translations.literal: The Liao harassed Xiongzhou; Shuowen was ordered to lead several tens of thousands of palace troops to the rescue; when he arrived the Liao fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao raided Xiongzhou, Shuowen was ordered to lead tens of thousands of palace troops to its relief; as soon as he arrived the Liao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，詔守文率兵屯三交，俄加領武州團練使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi Shuowen was ordered to lead troops to garrison Sanjiao; soon he was additionally given charge as regimental commissioner of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was ordered to garrison Sanjiao with his troops; soon afterward he was also made regimental commissioner of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬夏人擾攘，命守文帥師討之，破夏州鹽城鎮岌羅膩等十四族，斬首數千級，俘獲生畜萬計。

translations.literal: When the Xia people were in turmoil he was ordered to command troops against them; he defeated fourteen tribes including Jiluoni of Yancheng Town in Xiazhou, beheading several thousand and capturing livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut frontier grew turbulent he was ordered to lead a punitive campaign; he broke fourteen tribes including Jiluoni of Yancheng in Xiazhou, took several thousand heads, and captured livestock by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又破咩嵬族，殲焉。

translations.literal: He also defeated the Miewei tribe and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed the Miewei tribe, wiping them out entirely.

sentences.zh: 諸部畏懼，相率來降，凡銀、麟、夏三州歸附者百二十五族、萬六千餘戶，西鄙遂寧。

translations.literal: The various tribes were afraid and came to submit one after another; in all from the three prefectures of Yin, Lin, and Xia there submitted one hundred twenty-five tribes and more than sixteen thousand households, and the western border was then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were cowed and submitted in succession; in all one hundred twenty-five tribes and more than sixteen thousand households from Yin, Lin, and Xia came over, and the western frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 五年春，大舉北伐，為幽州道行營前軍步軍水陸都監。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, on the great northern expedition, he served as Overall Supervisor of Infantry and Naval Forces of the Vanguard on the Youzhou Route Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, during the great northern expedition, he served as overall supervisor of infantry and naval forces in the vanguard of the Youzhou route headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒與遼人遇，為流矢所中，氣色不撓，督戰益急，軍中服其量。

translations.literal: He suddenly encountered the Liao, was struck by a stray arrow, yet his bearing did not falter; he urged the battle on all the more fiercely, and the army admired his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly met the Liao army, was struck by a stray arrow, yet showed no dismay; he pressed the fight all the harder, and the troops admired his composure.

sentences.zh: 會大軍不利，坐違詔逗遛退軍，左遷右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the main army met with misfortune he was punished for disobeying the edict by lingering and withdrawing, and was demoted to Grand General of the Right Garrison Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army fared badly he was punished for disobeying orders by lingering and retreating, and was demoted to grand general of the Right Garrison Guards.

sentences.zh: 事具《曹彬傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is given in full in the biography of Cao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 明年復舊職，裁三月，拜宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to his former post; after only three months he was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored to his former post; after only three months he was appointed commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又與田欽祚並為北面排陣使，屯鎮州。

translations.literal: He was also made Northern Array Commissioner together with Tian Qinzuo and garrisoned Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Tian Qinzuo were jointly appointed northern array commissioners and garrisoned Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改南院使、鎮州路都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was changed to Southern Bureau Commissioner and Overall Deployer of the Zhenzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was made southern bureau commissioner and overall deployer of the Zhenzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 又為北面行營都部署兼鎮定、高陽關兩路排陣使。

translations.literal: He was also made Overall Deployer of the Northern Campaign Headquarters and concurrently Array Commissioner of the two routes of Zhending and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed overall deployer of the northern campaign headquarters and array commissioner for the Zhending and Gaoyang Pass circuits.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遼騎南侵，大破之唐河。

translations.literal: That winter Liao cavalry invaded southward and he inflicted a great defeat on them at the Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Liao cavalry raided southward, he routed them in a great victory on the Tang River.

sentences.zh: 端拱三年十月，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Duangong he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Duangong he died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 太宗悼惜之，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Taizong mourned and regretted his loss and posthumously gave him the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him deeply and posthumously granted him the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 諡忠武，追封譙王，遣中使護喪，歸葬京師。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Zhongwu and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao; a palace envoy was sent to escort the funeral and he was buried in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Zhongwu, "Loyal and Martial," and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao; a palace envoy escorted his remains home for burial in the capital.

sentences.zh: 守文沈厚有謀略，頗知書，每朝退，習書百行，出言溫雅，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: Shuowen was deep, steady, and resourceful, fairly learned in books; after each court session he would practice a hundred lines of calligraphy; his speech was mild and refined, and he never offended anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Shuowen was grave, steady, and shrewd, with a fair knowledge of letters; after each court session he practiced a hundred lines of calligraphy; his speech was mild and elegant, and he never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 先是，將臣戍邊者多致寇以邀戰功，河朔諸州殆無寧歲，既敗岐溝關，乃命守文以內職總兵鎮常山以經略之。

translations.literal: Earlier, generals garrisoning the frontier often provoked raiders to win battle merit; the prefectures of Hebei and Shuo scarcely had a peaceful year. After the defeat at Qigou Pass, Shuowen was ordered, as an inner-court official, to command troops and garrison Changshan to manage the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier commanders often provoked raids to win battle honors, and the Hebei-Shuo region knew scarcely a year of peace. After the defeat at Qigou Pass, Shuowen was sent as an inner-court official to command troops at Changshan and manage the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 守文既喪月餘，中使自北邊來言：「守文死，軍士皆流涕。

translations.literal: More than a month after Shuowen's death a palace envoy came from the northern frontier and said, "When Shuowen died, the soldiers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after Shuowen's death a palace envoy returned from the north and reported, "When Shuowen died, the soldiers all wept.

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「何以得此？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked, "How did he win this?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "How did he win such loyalty?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「守文得奉祿賜賚悉犒勞士卒，死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Shuowen used all his salary and gifts to reward the troops; on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Shuowen spent all his salary and imperial gifts rewarding the troops; when he died his family had nothing left."

sentences.zh: 」帝嗟歎久之，賜其家錢五百萬，為真宗納其女為夫人，即章穆皇后也。

translations.literal: " The emperor sighed in admiration for a long time, gave his family five million in cash, and had Zhenzong take his daughter as consort — she was Empress Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration for a long while, gave the family five million in cash, and had Zhenzong take his daughter as consort — she became Empress Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 子崇德，至太子中舍；

translations.literal: His son Chongde rose to be Middle Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongde rose to be middle household attendant of the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 崇信，至西京左藏庫使、同知皇城司，贈福州觀察使；

translations.literal: Chongxin rose to be Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury and Associate Director of the Imperial City Bureau, and was posthumously given the title of Military Commissioner of Fuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chongxin rose to be commissioner of the western-capital left treasury and associate director of the Imperial City Bureau, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 崇儼至崇儀使、全州刺史，贈潤州觀察使。

translations.literal: Chongyan rose to be Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and Prefect of Quanzhou, and was posthumously given the title of Military Commissioner of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyan rose to be honored ceremonial commissioner and prefect of Quanzhou, and was posthumously made military commissioner of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸司使無廢朝、贈官之例，崇信、崇儼咸以后兄故，特示優禮。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the various bureaus had no precedent for court mourning or posthumous titles; Chongxin and Chongyan both, because they were brothers of the empress, were specially shown exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners were not normally granted court mourning or posthumous titles; Chongxin and Chongyan received these exceptional honors because they were brothers of the empress.

sentences.zh: 崇德子承壽，至虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Chongde's son Shoushou rose to be Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chongde's son Shoushou rose to be an outer gentleman of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年，錄承壽子若水為太常寺奉禮郎，崇仁為解州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi, Shoushou's son Ruoshui was enrolled as Ceremonial Gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Chongren as Regimental Commissioner of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianxi, Shoushou's son Ruoshui was enrolled as a ceremonial gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Chongren as regimental commissioner of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 尹崇珂

translations.literal: Yin Chongke
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chongke

sentences.zh: 宋初，出為淄州刺史，有善政，民詣闕請刻石頌德，太祖命殿中侍御史李穆撰文賜之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he went out as Prefect of Zizhou; his governance was good, and the people came to court requesting a stone inscription to praise his virtue; Taizu ordered Palace Attendant Censor Li Mu to compose the text and bestow it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was posted as prefect of Zizhou, where his rule was benevolent; the people came to court to request a stone inscription in his praise, and Taizu ordered Palace Attendant Censor Li Mu to compose the text and grant it to them.

sentences.zh: 討湖南，為行營前軍馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Hunan he served as Overall Commander of Cavalry of the Vanguard on the Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hunan campaign he served as overall commander of cavalry in the campaign vanguard.

sentences.zh: 荊湘平，授朗州團練使。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang were pacified he was given the post of Regimental Commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing and Xiang were pacified he was appointed regimental commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 又與潘美、丁德裕克郴州。

translations.literal: Together with Pan Mei and Ding Deyu he captured Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Pan Mei and Ding Deyu he captured Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，征嶺表，以崇珂為行營馬步軍副部署。

translations.literal: During Qiande, on the campaign in Lingwai, Chongke was made Deputy Deployer of Horse and Foot Forces on the Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, on the Lingnan campaign, Chongke was made deputy deployer of horse and foot forces on the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 克廣州，擒劉鋹，即日詔與潘美同知廣州兼市舶轉運等使，錄功遷保信軍節度。

translations.literal: Guangzhou was taken and Liu Chang captured; that same day an edict made Chongke and Pan Mei joint administrators of Guangzhou, concurrently commissioners of maritime trade and transport, and for recorded merit he was promoted to military governor of the Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzhou fell and Liu Chang was captured, an edict that same day appointed Chongke and Pan Mei joint administrators of Guangzhou with charge of maritime trade and transport; for his recorded merit he was promoted to military governor of the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南漢開府樂範、容州都指揮使鄧存忠、韶州賊帥周思瓊、春恩道都指揮使麥漢瓊等據五州之地以叛。

translations.literal: Before long, Le Fan of the Southern Han Secretariat, Deng Cunzhong overall commander of Rongzhou, the bandit chief Zhou Siqiong of Shaozhou, Mai Hanqiong overall commander of Chun'en Circuit, and others held five prefectures in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Le Fan of the Southern Han secretariat, Deng Cunzhong commander of Rongzhou, the bandit leader Zhou Siqiong of Shaozhou, Mai Hanqiong commander of Chun'en Circuit, and others seized five prefectures and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 崇珂討之，太祖遣中使李神祐督戰，數月盡平其黨，還治所。

translations.literal: Chongke campaigned against them; Taizu sent Palace Envoy Li Shenyou to supervise the fighting, and within several months all their factions were pacified; he returned to his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: Chongke campaigned against them; Taizu sent Palace Envoy Li Shenyou to supervise the fighting, and within a few months their factions were all suppressed; Chongke then returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護其喪，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: A palace envoy was sent to escort his funeral, and he was buried in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy escorted his remains home for burial in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以其子昭吉、弟崇珪並為西京作坊使，昭吉領會州刺史，崇珪領歙州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoji and younger brother Chonggui were both made Commissioners of the Western Capital Workshops; Zhaoji was given charge of Huizhou as prefect and Chonggui of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoji and younger brother Chonggui were both appointed commissioners of the western-capital workshops; Zhaoji was made prefect of Huizhou and Chonggui of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗在周朝娶崇珂妹，追諡淑德皇后。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizong was in the Zhou dynasty he married Chongke's younger sister, who was posthumously given the title Empress Shude.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still in the Zhou court, Taizong had married Chongke's younger sister, who was later posthumously titled Empress Shude.

sentences.zh: 昭吉至洛苑使。

translations.literal: Zhaoji rose to be Commissioner of the Luoyang Park.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoji rose to be commissioner of the Luoyang imperial park.

sentences.zh: 次子昭輯，至供奉官、閤閣門祗候。

translations.literal: His second son Zhaoji rose to be Palace Attendant and Gate Attendant of the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhaoji rose to be a palace attendant and inner-gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓，字光乂，其先涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang, styled Guangyi, was by origin a man of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang, styled Guangyi, was descended from a family of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁恭，唐盧龍軍節度。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rengong was military governor of the Lulong Army under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rengong was military governor of the Lulong Army under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖守文，襲滄州盧彥威，遂據其城，昭宗授以節鉞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouwen attacked Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou, seized the city, and Emperor Zhaozong granted him the commander's seal.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouwen overthrew Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou, seized the city, and Emperor Zhaozong invested him with the commander's seal.

sentences.zh: 後其弟守光囚父仁恭，守文舉兵討之，軍敗，為守光所殺。

translations.literal: Later his younger brother Shouguang imprisoned their father Rengong; Shouwen raised troops against him, was defeated, and was killed by Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his brother Shouguang imprisoned their father Rengong; Shouwen raised troops against him, was defeated, and was killed by Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 廷讓與其父延進避難南奔。

translations.literal: Tingrang and his father Yanjin fled south to escape the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang and his father Yanjin fled south to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 少有膂力，周祖鎮鄴，以隸帳下。

translations.literal: In youth he had great physical strength; when the Zhou founder garrisoned Ye he was placed under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was powerfully built; when the Zhou founder garrisoned Ye he was taken into his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補內殿直押班，累遷龍捷都校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed to the Inner Palace Direct Escort Class and was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Dragon Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed to the inner-palace direct escort class and rose to colonel of the Dragon Swift Army.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征淮南，以功領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong on the Huainan campaign and for merit was given charge of Leizhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong on the Huainan campaign and, for his achievements, was made prefect of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷涪州團練使、領鐵騎右廂。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Regimental Commissioner of Fuzhou and given command of the Right Wing of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to regimental commissioner of Fuzhou and given command of the right wing of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宋初，轉江州防禦使、領龍捷右廂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to Defender of Jiangzhou and given command of the Right Wing of the Dragon Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was made defender of Jiangzhou and given command of the right wing of the Dragon Swift Army.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，為行營先鋒使。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Yun he served as Vanguard Commissioner of the Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Yun he served as vanguard commissioner of the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領江寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was changed to Overall Commander of the Palace Cavalry and given charge as military governor of the Jiangning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was made overall commander of the palace cavalry and military governor of the Jiangning Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年春，詔領兵赴潞州，以備幷寇。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Qiande he was ordered to lead troops to Luzhou to guard against Bingzhou raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Qiande he was ordered to lead troops to Luzhou to guard against raids from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，興師伐蜀，為四川行營前軍兵馬副都部署，率禁兵步騎萬人、諸州兵萬人，由歸州進討。

translations.literal: That winter an army was raised against Shu; he served as Deputy Overall Deployer of Horse and Foot Forces of the Vanguard on the Sichuan Route Campaign Headquarters, leading ten thousand palace infantry and cavalry and ten thousand troops from various prefectures to advance from Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the Shu campaign, he served as deputy overall deployer of the Sichuan route vanguard, leading ten thousand palace horse and foot troops and ten thousand men from the prefectures in an advance from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 入其境，連破松木、三會、巫山等砦，獲蜀將南光海等五千餘人，擒戰棹都指揮使袁德宏等千二百人，奪戰艦二百餘艘。

translations.literal: Entering their territory he successively took the stockades of Songmu, Sanhui, Wushan, and others, capturing more than five thousand men including the Shu general Nan Guanghai, seizing twelve hundred men including the battle-oar overall commander Yuan Dehong, and taking more than two hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Shu territory he took the stockades at Songmu, Sanhui, Wushan, and elsewhere in succession, capturing more than five thousand men including the Shu general Nan Guanghai, taking twelve hundred men including battle-oar commander Yuan Dehong, and seizing more than two hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 又獲水軍三千人，因度南岸，斬三千餘級。

translations.literal: He also captured three thousand naval troops, then crossed to the south bank and beheaded more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured three thousand naval troops, crossed to the south bank, and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 初，夔州有鎖鏁江為浮梁，上設敵棚三重，夾江列礮具。

translations.literal: Earlier at Kuizhou the Suoluo River had been chained to form a floating bridge, with three tiers of fighting sheds above and artillery ranged along both banks.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuizhou the Suoluo River had been chained into a floating bridge with three tiers of fighting sheds above and artillery lined along both banks.

sentences.zh: 廷讓等將行，太祖以地圖示之，指鏁江曰：「我軍至此，泝流而上，慎勿以舟師爭勝，當先以步騎陸行，出其不意擊之，俟其勢卻，即以戰棹夾攻，取之必矣。

translations.literal: As Tingrang and the others were about to depart, Taizu showed them a map, pointed to the Suoluo River, and said, "When our army reaches here and moves upstream, be careful not to seek victory with the fleet alone; you should first march infantry and cavalry overland and strike by surprise. When their force recoils, then attack with warships from both sides — you are sure to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tingrang's departure Taizu showed him a map, pointed to the Suoluo River, and said, "When our army reaches here and moves upstream, do not try to win by naval battle alone. March infantry and cavalry overland first and strike by surprise; when the enemy recoils, attack with warships from both sides and you are sure to take it.

sentences.zh: 」及師至，距鏁江三十里，舍舟步進，先奪其橋，復牽舟而上，破州城，守將高彥儔自焚，悉如太祖計。

translations.literal: " When the army arrived, thirty li from the Suoluo River they abandoned the boats and advanced on foot, first seizing the bridge, then hauling the boats upstream, breaking the prefectural city; the defending general Gao Yanfu burned himself — all exactly as Taizu had planned.
translations.idiomatic: When the army arrived, thirty li from the river they left the boats and marched overland, seized the bridge first, then hauled the fleet upstream and stormed the city; the defender Gao Yanfu burned himself to death — exactly as Taizu had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 遂進克萬、施、開、忠四州，峽中郡縣悉下。

translations.literal: He then advanced and took the four prefectures of Wan, Shi, Kai, and Zhong; all the counties of the Gorges submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Wan, Shi, Kai, and Zhong, and all the counties of the Gorges fell.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，次遂州，州將陳俞率吏民來降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he halted at Suizhou; the prefectural commander Chen Yu led officials and people to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he reached Suizhou, where the commander Chen Yu led officials and people in surrender.

sentences.zh: 盡出府庫金帛以給將士。

translations.literal: He emptied the treasury of gold and silk to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied the prefectural treasury of gold and silk to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 初出師也，太祖命之曰：「所得郡縣，當傾帑藏，為朕賞戰士，國家所收唯土疆爾。

translations.literal: When the army first set out Taizu had ordered him, "In every prefecture and county you take, empty the treasuries to reward the warriors for me; what the state receives is only the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Before the campaign Taizu had told him, "In every prefecture and county you take, empty the treasuries to reward the troops for me; the state wants only the land.

sentences.zh: 」故人皆效命，所至成功。

translations.literal: " Therefore everyone gave their utmost, and wherever he went he succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Men gave their utmost, and wherever he went he succeeded.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，王全斌等皆坐縱部下掠奪子女玉帛及納賄賂左降，惟廷讓秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, Wang Quanbin and others were all punished for letting their subordinates plunder women, children, jade, and silk and for taking bribes, being demoted — only Tingrang had not taken so much as a hair.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, Wang Quanbin and others were demoted for letting their men plunder people and goods and for taking bribes; only Tingrang had taken nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 及全師雄等作亂，郡縣相應，寇盜蠭起。

translations.literal: When Quan Shixiong and others rebelled, prefectures and counties rose in response and bandits swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Shixiong and others rebelled, prefectures and counties joined them and bandits swarmed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 廷讓又與曹彬破之，以功改領鎮安軍節度，從征太原。

translations.literal: Tingrang again joined Cao Bin in defeating them; for merit he was changed to military governor of the Zhen'an Army and followed the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang joined Cao Bin in crushing the revolt; for his merit he was made military governor of the Zhen'an Army and took part in the campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，出為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he went out as military governor of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was posted as military governor of the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，入為右驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he entered court as General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was recalled to court as general-in-chief of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，曹彬敗於岐溝關，諸將失律，多坐黜免。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi Cao Bin was defeated at Qigou Pass; the generals had violated discipline and many were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi Cao Bin was defeated at Qigou Pass; many generals who had broken discipline were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹擾邊，時議遣將，無愜上意者。

translations.literal: Soon the Khitan harassed the frontier; at court they discussed sending generals, but none pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan raided the frontier; court discussion turned to sending generals, but none satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時廷讓與宋偓、張永德並罷節鎮在環列，帝欲令擊契丹自效，乃遣分守邊郡，以廷讓知雄州，又徙瀛州兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: At that time Tingrang, Song Wo, and Zhang Yongde had all been removed from their military governorships and stood in the imperial circle; the emperor wished them to strike the Khitan and redeem themselves, so he sent them to guard frontier prefectures separately — Tingrang was made administrator of Xiongzhou and then transferred to Overall Deployer of Horse and Foot Forces at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang, Song Wo, and Zhang Yongde had all lost their commands and stood at court; the emperor wanted them to redeem themselves against the Khitan, so he sent them to frontier posts — Tingrang as administrator of Xiongzhou, then as overall deployer of horse and foot forces at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹數萬騎來侵，廷讓與戰君子館。

translations.literal: That winter tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen invaded; Tingrang fought them at Junzi Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: That winter tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen invaded, and Tingrang met them in battle at Junzi Lodge.

sentences.zh: 時天大寒，兵士弓弩皆不能彀，契丹圍廷讓數重。

translations.literal: The weather was bitterly cold; the soldiers' bows and crossbows could not be drawn, and the Khitan surrounded Tingrang in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The cold was so severe that the men's bows and crossbows could not be drawn, and the Khitan surrounded Tingrang in layer after layer.

sentences.zh: 廷讓先分精兵屬李繼隆為後殿，緩急為援。

translations.literal: Tingrang had earlier detached elite troops under Li Jilong as rearguard to aid him in emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrang had earlier detached elite troops under Li Jilong as rearguard to support him if needed.

sentences.zh: 至是，繼隆退保樂壽，廷讓一軍皆沒，死者數萬人，僅以數騎獲免。

translations.literal: At this point Jilong withdrew to hold Leshou; Tingrang's entire army was destroyed, tens of thousands died, and he escaped with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jilong then withdrew to Leshou; Tingrang's whole force was wiped out, tens of thousands were killed, and he escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 先鋒將賀令圖、楊重進皆陷於契丹。

translations.literal: The vanguard generals He Lingtu and Yang Chongjin both fell into Khitan hands.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard generals He Lingtu and Yang Chongjin were both captured by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 自是河朔戍兵無鬥志，又科鄉民為兵以守城，皆未習戰鬥。

translations.literal: From this time the garrison troops of Hebei and Shuo had no fighting spirit; village people were also conscripted as soldiers to defend cities, and none were trained for battle.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Hebei-Shuo garrisons lost their will to fight; villagers were conscripted to hold the cities, and none were trained for combat.

sentences.zh: 契丹遂長驅而入，陷深、祁、德數州，殺官吏，俘士民，所在輦金帛而去。

translations.literal: The Khitan then drove deep inland, taking several prefectures including Shen, Qi, and De, killing officials, capturing commoners, and everywhere carting off gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then swept deep into the country, taking Shen, Qi, De, and other prefectures, killing officials, capturing civilians, and carting off gold and silk wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 博、魏之北，民尤苦焉。

translations.literal: North of Bo and Wei the people suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: The people north of Bo and Wei suffered most of all.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，下哀痛之詔。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he issued an edict of grief and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it he issued an edict of mourning and grief.

sentences.zh: 初，廷讓詣闕待罪，太宗知為李繼隆所誤，不之責。

translations.literal: Earlier Tingrang had come to court to await punishment; Taizong knew he had been misled by Li Jilong and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingrang first came to court to await punishment, Taizong knew Li Jilong had misled him and did not hold him responsible.

sentences.zh: 四年，復命代張永德知雄州兼兵馬部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again ordered to replace Zhang Yongde as administrator of Xiongzhou and concurrent deployer of horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again ordered to replace Zhang Yongde as administrator of Xiongzhou with charge of horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 是秋以疾聞，帝遣內醫診視，因上言求歸京師，不俟報，乃離屯所。

translations.literal: That autumn his illness was reported; the emperor sent a palace physician to examine him; he then memorialized asking to return to the capital, and without awaiting a reply left his garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn word of his illness reached court; the emperor sent a palace physician to examine him; Tingrang then asked to return to the capital and, without waiting for a reply, left his post.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下御史按問，獄具。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered the censorate to investigate; the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered the censorate to investigate; the case was proved.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「右驍衛上將軍劉廷讓，朕以其宿舊，曾董軍政，擢自環尹，付之成師，俾控邊關，式防寇鈔。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Liu Tingrang, General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards — because he was an old companion I once put him in charge of military affairs, raised him from the imperial circle, entrusted him with a full army, and set him to control the frontier passes and guard against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Liu Tingrang, general-in-chief of the Right Martial Guards — as an old companion I once placed him in charge of military affairs, raised him from the imperial circle, entrusted him with a full army, and set him to hold the frontier passes against raiders.

sentences.zh: 而乃以病為解，不俟報命，委棄戎重，俶裝上道。

translations.literal: Yet he used illness as an excuse, did not await orders, abandoned his military charge, and set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he pleaded illness, left without awaiting orders, abandoned his military command, and set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 矧萬旅所集，實制於中權，列燧相望，或虞於外侮。

translations.literal: Moreover tens of thousands of troops were gathered, with real control in the central command; beacon towers stood in sight of one another, and there was fear of foreign attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of troops were gathered under central command; beacon towers stood in sight of one another, and the frontier was exposed to attack.

sentences.zh: 事機一失，咎責安歸？

translations.literal: Once the opportunity was lost, to whom would blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: Once the moment was lost, on whom would blame fall?

sentences.zh: 有司議刑，當在不赦。

translations.literal: The responsible offices discussed punishment and held that he should not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices held that his offense deserved no pardon.

sentences.zh: 錄其素效，特從寬典，可削奪在身官爵，配隸商州。

translations.literal: Recording his long service, we specially apply lenient law: his current offices and titles are to be stripped and he is to be assigned to Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In view of his long service we apply leniency: strip his offices and titles and assign him to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」又黜其子如京使永德為濠州團練副使，崇儀副使永和為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: " His sons were also demoted: Yongde, a commissioner on capital duty, to Vice Regimental Commissioner of Haozhou, and Yonghe, Vice Honored Ceremonial Commissioner, to Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were also demoted: Yongde, a capital commissioner, to vice regimental commissioner of Haozhou, and Yonghe, vice honored ceremonial commissioner, to prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷讓既黜，怏怏不食，行至華州卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: After Tingrang was demoted he was resentful and would not eat; on the road he died at Huazhou, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion Tingrang brooded and refused to eat; he died on the road at Huazhou at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝錄其舊勳，贈太師。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his old merit and posthumously gave him the title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored his past service and posthumously granted him the title of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子永德，至內殿崇班；

translations.literal: His son Yongde rose to be Honored Class of the Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongde rose to honored class of the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 永恭，至西京作坊副使；

translations.literal: Yonggong rose to be Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops;
translations.idiomatic: Yonggong rose to vice commissioner of the western-capital workshops;

sentences.zh: 永和，為內殿承制；

translations.literal: Yonghe became Inner Palace Drafter;
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe became an inner-palace drafter;

sentences.zh: 永錫，至崇班；

translations.literal: Yongxi rose to Honored Class;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi rose to honored class;

sentences.zh: 永保、永昌、永規並至閤門祗候；

translations.literal: Yongbao, Yongchang, and Yonggui all rose to Gate Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Yongbao, Yongchang, and Yonggui all became gate attendants;

sentences.zh: 永崇，為崇班；

translations.literal: Yongchong became Honored Class;
translations.idiomatic: Yongchong held honored class;

sentences.zh: 永寧及孫允忠並為閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Yongning and his grandson Yunzhong both became Gate Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning and his grandson Yunzhong both became gate attendants.

sentences.zh: 袁繼忠

translations.literal: Yuan Jizhong
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jizhong

sentences.zh: 袁繼忠，其先振武人，後徙幷州。

translations.literal: Yuan Jizhong — his ancestors were from Zhenwu and later moved to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jizhong's family was originally from Zhenwu and later moved to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父進，仕周為階州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Jin served the Zhou as Defender of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin served the Zhou as defender of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 繼忠以父任補右班殿直。

translations.literal: Jizhong entered service through his father's position as Right Class Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong entered service through his father's office and was appointed a right-class palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖平澤、潞，討幷、汾，悉預攻戰。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Ze and Lu and campaigned against Bing and Fen, he took part in all the attacks.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Ze and Lu and campaigned against Bing and Fen, Jizhong took part in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 乾德中征蜀，隸大將劉廷讓麾下。

translations.literal: During Qiande, on the Shu campaign, he served under the great general Liu Tingrang.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, on the Shu campaign, he served under Liu Tingrang.

sentences.zh: 既克蜀，知雲安軍，歷嘉、蜀二州監軍。

translations.literal: After Shu was taken he administered Yun'an Army and successively served as military supervisor of Jia and Shu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he administered Yun'an Army and served as military supervisor of Jia and Shu prefectures in turn.

sentences.zh: 開寶中伐廣南，為先鋒壕砦。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, on the campaign against Guangnan, he served as vanguard trench stockade commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, on the Guangnan campaign, he commanded the vanguard trench stockades.

sentences.zh: 廣南平，以功遷供奉官，護隰州白壁關屯兵。

translations.literal: When Guangnan was pacified he was promoted to Palace Attendant for merit and escorted the garrison at Baiyu Pass in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangnan was pacified he was promoted to palace attendant for his merit and given charge of the garrison at Baiyu Pass in Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河東拒命，繼忠累入其境，破三砦，擒將校二人，得生口、馬牛羊、鎧仗逾萬計。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong resisted orders; Jizhong repeatedly entered their territory, took three stockades, captured two officers, and obtained captives, horses, cattle, sheep, and armor and weapons numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: While Hedong still resisted the throne, Jizhong repeatedly raided its territory, took three stockades, captured two officers, and seized captives, livestock, and arms numbering more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 近戍主將懼無功受譴，以誠告繼忠，繼忠以所獲分與之，遂與都巡檢郭進略地忻、代州，改天平軍巡檢。

translations.literal: The nearby garrison commander feared punishment for lack of achievement and frankly told Jizhong; Jizhong shared his captures with him, then joined Overall Inspector Guo Jin in raiding Xin and Daizhou, and was changed to Inspector of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: The nearby garrison commander, fearing punishment for lack of results, confided in Jizhong; Jizhong shared his spoils with him, then joined overall inspector Guo Jin in raiding Xin and Daizhou, and was made inspector of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以為閤門祗候，令擊梅山洞賊，破之。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was made Gate Attendant and ordered to attack the bandits of Meishan Cave; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he was made a gate attendant and ordered to attack the bandits of Meishan Cave; he routed them.

sentences.zh: 又巡遏邊部於唐龍鎮。

translations.literal: He also patrolled and restrained frontier tribes at Tanglong Town.
translations.idiomatic: He also patrolled the frontier tribes at Tanglong Town.

sentences.zh: 太宗征太原，繼忠預破鷹揚軍，先登陷陣。

translations.literal: On Taizong's campaign against Taiyuan, Jizhong beforehand broke the Eagle Soaring Army and was first to scale the walls and break the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's Taiyuan campaign, Jizhong first broke the Eagle Soaring Army and was the first to scale the walls and break into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 契丹入代境，繼忠率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Dai territory Jizhong led troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Dai territory Jizhong led troops and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 以功遷通事舍人，護高陽關屯兵。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Memorial Presenter and escorted the garrison at Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to memorial presenter and given charge of the garrison at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 與崔彥進破契丹長城口，殺獲數萬眾，璽書褒美。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Yanjin he defeated the Khitan at Changcheng Pass, killing and capturing tens of thousands; an imperial letter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: With Cui Yanjin he defeated the Khitan at Changcheng Pass, killing and capturing tens of thousands; the emperor sent a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 時有勸繼忠自論其功者，繼忠不答。

translations.literal: At the time some urged Jizhong to plead his own merit; he did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jizhong to petition for recognition of his merit; he made no reply.

sentences.zh: 會趙保忠來朝獻其地，綏州刺史李克憲偃蹇不奉詔，遣繼忠諭旨，竟率克憲入朝。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong came to court to offer his territory, Li Kexian, Prefect of Suizhou, was arrogant and would not obey the edict; Jizhong was sent to convey the imperial will and in the end led Kexian to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong came to court to offer his territory, Suizhou prefect Li Kexian defied the edict; Jizhong was sent to convey the imperial will and eventually brought Kexian to court.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Western Upper Gate Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to western upper gate vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔與田仁朗率兵定河西諸州，大破西人於葭蘆州，遷引進副使，護定州屯兵。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Tian Renlang to lead troops to pacify the prefectures west of the river; he inflicted a great defeat on the western peoples at Jialu Prefecture, was promoted to Vice Introducing Commissioner, and escorted the garrison at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Tian Renlang to pacify the Hexi prefectures; he routed the western forces at Jialu Prefecture, was promoted to vice introducing commissioner, and took charge of the garrison at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted to western upper gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，大將田重進征契丹，命繼忠為定州路行營馬步軍都監。

translations.literal: In the third year the great general Tian Chongjin campaigned against the Khitan; Jizhong was ordered to be Overall Supervisor of Horse and Foot Forces on the Dingzhou Route Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on General Tian Chongjin's Khitan campaign, Jizhong was made overall supervisor of horse and foot forces on the Dingzhou route headquarters.

sentences.zh: 領師取飛狐，下靈丘，平蔚州，擒其帥大鵬翼以獻，事見《重進傳》。

translations.literal: He led the army to take Feihu, reduce Lingqiu, pacify Weizhou, and capture their commander Dapengyi to present; the affair is given in the biography of Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army to take Feihu, reduce Lingqiu, pacify Weizhou, and capture the commander Dapengyi as a prize; the full account appears in the biography of Tian Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 師還，繼忠為後殿，行列甚整。

translations.literal: When the army returned Jizhong served as rearguard and the ranks were very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Jizhong commanded the rearguard, and the ranks remained perfectly orderly.

sentences.zh: 至定州，重進欲斬降卒後期至者，繼忠諭以殺降不祥，皆救免之。

translations.literal: At Dingzhou Chongjin wished to behead surrendered soldiers who arrived late; Jizhong urged that killing those who had submitted was inauspicious, and all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou Chongjin wanted to execute surrendered soldiers who arrived late; Jizhong argued that killing men who had submitted was ill-omened, and all were spared.

sentences.zh: 遷判四方館事、領播州刺史，護屯兵如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to handle affairs of the Four Directions Bureau and given charge of Bozhou as prefect, continuing to escort the garrison as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to handle affairs of the Four Directions Bureau and appointed prefect of Bozhou, while continuing to command the garrison as before.

sentences.zh: 大將李繼隆以易州靜塞騎兵尤驍果，取隸麾下，畜其妻子城中。

translations.literal: The great general Li Jilong, because the Jingse Cavalry of Yizhou were especially fierce and able, took them under his command and kept their wives and children in the city.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Jilong, because the Jingse Cavalry of Yizhou were especially fierce, took them under his command and kept their families in the city.

sentences.zh: 繼忠言於繼隆曰：「此精卒，止可守城，萬一敵至，城中誰與悍者？

translations.literal: Jizhong said to Jilong, "These elite troops should only defend the city — if the enemy comes, who in the city will fight fiercely?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong told Jilong, "These elite troops should stay to defend the city — if the enemy comes, who in the city will fight them off?

sentences.zh: 」繼隆不從。

translations.literal: " Jilong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹入寇，城陷，卒妻子皆為所俘。

translations.literal: Soon the Khitan invaded; the city fell and the soldiers' wives and children were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan invaded; the city fell and the soldiers' families were all captured.

sentences.zh: 繼隆疑此卒怨己，欲分隸諸軍。

translations.literal: Jilong suspected these soldiers resented him and wished to distribute them among various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong suspected the men blamed him and wanted to scatter them among other units.

sentences.zh: 繼忠曰：「不可，但奏升其軍額，優以廩給，使之盡節可也。

translations.literal: Jizhong said, "That will not do — only memorialize to raise their army quota, treat them generously with rations, and they will give their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong said, "You must not — only petition to raise their army quota, pay them generously, and they will serve with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 」從之，眾皆感悅。

translations.literal: " He followed this advice and all were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong followed his advice and the men were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 繼忠因自請以隸麾下。

translations.literal: Jizhong then asked on his own to have them placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong then asked to take them under his own command.

sentences.zh: 會契丹騎大至，駐唐河北，諸將欲堅壁待之。

translations.literal: When Khitan horsemen came in great force and halted north of the Tang River, the generals wished to hold the walls and wait.
translations.idiomatic: When a large Khitan force arrived and camped north of the Tang River, the generals wanted to hold the walls and wait.

sentences.zh: 繼忠曰：「今強敵在近，城中屯重兵不能剪滅，令長驅深入，侵略他郡，雖欲謀自安之計，豈折衝禦侮之用乎？

translations.literal: Jizhong said, "Now a strong enemy is near and we hold a heavy garrison in the city yet cannot destroy them — if we let them drive deep and invade other prefectures, even if we seek a plan for our own safety, how is that the use of breaking the enemy charge and repelling insult?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong said, "A strong enemy is at our gates and we hold a large garrison yet cannot destroy them — if we let them sweep inland and ravage other prefectures, how does holding the walls serve to break the enemy and defend the realm?

sentences.zh: 我將身先士卒，死於寇矣！

translations.literal: I will lead the troops in person and die at the hands of the raiders!
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the charge in person and die fighting the enemy if I must!

sentences.zh: 」辭氣慷慨，眾壯之。

translations.literal: " His words were ardent and the troops took heart.
translations.idiomatic: His words were fierce and the troops took heart.

sentences.zh: 靜塞軍摧鋒先入，契丹兵大潰。

translations.literal: The Jingse Army broke the enemy vanguard and entered first; the Khitan army collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingse Army broke the enemy vanguard and led the charge; the Khitan army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，降璽書獎諭，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he sent an imperial letter of reward and praise and gave very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it he sent an imperial letter of commendation and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，遷引進使，護鎮定、高陽關兩路屯兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was promoted to Introducing Commissioner and escorted the garrisons of the two routes of Zhending and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua he was promoted to introducing commissioner and given charge of the garrisons on the Zhending and Gaoyang Pass circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年，被病，召赴闕，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the third year he fell ill, was summoned to court, and died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill, was summoned to court, and died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 繼忠長厚忠謹，士大夫多與遊，前後賜賚鉅萬計，悉以犒賞士卒。

translations.literal: Jizhong was generous, steady, loyal, and careful; many scholar-officials associated with him; gifts before and after totaled tens of thousands, all used to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong was generous, loyal, and careful; many scholar-officials sought his company; imperial gifts totaling tens of thousands he spent entirely on rewarding the troops.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，家無餘財，搢紳稱之。

translations.literal: On the day he died his household had no surplus wealth, and the gentry praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his family had nothing left, and the gentry praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子用成，雍熙初登進士第，至太常博士。

translations.literal: His son Yongcheng passed the jinshi examination at the beginning of Yongxi and rose to be Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongcheng passed the jinshi examination early in Yongxi and rose to be a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 崔彥進

translations.literal: Cui Yanjin
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanjin

sentences.zh: 崔彥進，大名人。

translations.literal: Cui Yanjin was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanjin was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 純質有膽略，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was plain and honest, with courage and resource, skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and honest by nature, he was bold and resourceful and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，隸周祖帳下。

translations.literal: During Qianyou of Han he served under the Zhou founder's banner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of the Later Han he entered the Zhou founder's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補衛士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed a palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵，令領禁兵以從。

translations.literal: When Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan he was ordered to lead palace troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan he was ordered to lead palace troops in his train.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，為控鶴指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he became Commander of the Crane Control Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiande he became commander of the Crane Control Army.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，以功遷散員都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed the Huainan campaign and for merit was promoted to Overall Deputy of the Loose Members.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huainan campaign he was promoted for merit to overall deputy of the loose members.

sentences.zh: 從平瓦橋關，改東西班指揮使、領昭州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Waqiao Pass and was changed to Commander of the Eastern and Western Classes and given charge of Shaozhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Waqiao Pass and was made commander of the eastern and western classes and prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改控鶴右廂指揮使、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was changed to Commander of the Right Wing of the Crane Control Army and given charge as Regimental Commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was made commander of the right wing of the Crane Control Army and regimental commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 征李筠，為先鋒部署，以功遷常州防禦使。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Yun he served as Vanguard Deployer and for merit was promoted to Defender of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Yun he served as vanguard deployer and was promoted to defender of Changzhou for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 從平李重進，改虎捷右廂。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Li Chongjin and was changed to the Right Wing of the Tiger Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Li Chongjin and was transferred to the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was promoted to Overall Commander of the Palace Infantry and given charge as military governor of the Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he was made overall commander of the palace infantry and military governor of the Wuxin Army.

sentences.zh: 大舉伐蜀，為鳳州路行營前軍副都部署。

translations.literal: On the great campaign against Shu he served as Deputy Overall Deployer of the Vanguard on the Fengzhou Route Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the great Shu campaign he served as deputy overall deployer of the Fengzhou route vanguard.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，坐縱部下略玉帛、子女及諸不法事，左遷昭化軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was punished for letting his subordinates plunder jade, silk, women, and children and for various unlawful acts, and was demoted to Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army with retention of post.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was demoted for letting his men plunder goods and people and for other illegal acts, and was made military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhaohua Army with retention of post.

sentences.zh: 太祖郊祀西洛，彥進來朝，授彰信軍節度。

translations.literal: When Taizu performed suburban sacrifice in western Luoyang, Yanjin came to court and was given the post of military governor of the Zhangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu performed the suburban sacrifice in western Luoyang, Yanjin came to court and was appointed military governor of the Zhangxin Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，移鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to garrison Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to command at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遣將征太原，分命攻城，以彥進與郢州防禦使尹勳攻其東，彰德軍節度李漢瓊、冀州刺史牛思進攻其南，桂州觀察使曹翰、翰林使杜彥圭攻其西，彰信軍節度劉遇、光州刺史史珪攻其北。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year generals were sent to campaign against Taiyuan and assigned to attack the city separately: Yanjin with Yin Xun, Defender of Yingzhou, attacked the east; Li Hanqiong, military governor of the Zhangde Army, and Niu Sijin, Prefect of Ji, attacked the south; Cao Han, Military Commissioner of Guizhou, and Hanlin Commissioner Du Yangui attacked the west; Liu Yu, military governor of the Zhangxin Army, and Shi Gui, Prefect of Guang, attacked the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year generals were dispatched against Taiyuan with separate assaults: Yanjin and Yin Xun, defender of Yingzhou, attacked from the east; Li Hanqiong and Niu Sijin from the south; Cao Han and Du Yangui from the west; Liu Yu and Shi Gui from the north.

sentences.zh: 彥進督戰甚急，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Yanjin pressed the fighting very hard and Taizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin pressed the assault vigorously, and Taizu commended him.

sentences.zh: 晉陽平，從征幽州，又與內供奉官江守鈞率兵攻城之西北。

translations.literal: When Jinyang was pacified he followed the campaign against Youzhou and again with Inner Palace Attendant Jiang Shoujun led troops to attack the northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinyang fell he joined the Youzhou campaign and, with Inner Palace Attendant Jiang Shoujun, led the assault on the northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 及班師，詔彥進與西上閤門副使薛繼興、閤門祗候李守斌領兵屯關南，以功加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the army returned Yanjin was ordered with Western Upper Gate Vice Commissioner Xue Jixing and Gate Attendant Li Shoubin to lead troops to garrison south of the passes; for merit he was given the additional title of Grand Marshal with nominal commission.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Yanjin was ordered with Xue Jixing and Li Shoubin to garrison the region south of the passes; for his achievements he was given the additional title of honorary grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 是秋，契丹侵遂城，彥進與劉廷翰、崔翰等擊破之，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: That autumn the Khitan invaded Suicheng; Yanjin with Liu Tinghan, Cui Han, and others defeated them and took ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the Khitan raided Suicheng, Yanjin with Liu Tinghan, Cui Han, and others routed them and took ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕北巡，以彥進為關南都部署，敗契丹於唐興口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage toured north; Yanjin was made Overall Deployer south of the passes and defeated the Khitan at Tangxing Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, during the northern tour, Yanjin was made overall deployer south of the passes and defeated the Khitan at Tangxing Ford.

sentences.zh: 彥進頻立戰功，然好聚財貨，所至無善政。

translations.literal: Yanjin repeatedly won battle merit, yet he loved to amass wealth; wherever he went his governance was not good.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin won repeated battle honors, but he loved to amass wealth and governed poorly wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 沒後，諸子爭家財，有司攝治。

translations.literal: After his death his sons disputed the family property and the responsible offices took charge of the case.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his sons fought over the family estate, and the authorities took up the case.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，為決之，謂左右曰：「此細務，朕不宜親臨，但以彥進嘗任節制，不欲令其子辱於父耳。」

translations.literal: Taizong summoned them, decided the matter, and said to his attendants, "This is a minor affair and I ought not to attend to it in person, but because Yanjin once held a military governorship I do not wish his sons to disgrace their father."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned them, settled the dispute, and told his attendants, "This is a trifling matter and I should not handle it myself, but because Yanjin once held a command I do not want his sons to disgrace their father."

sentences.zh: 子懷遵，至內殿崇班；

translations.literal: His son Huaizun rose to Honored Class of the Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaizun rose to honored class of the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 懷清，至崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Huaqing rose to Vice Honored Ceremonial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Huaqing rose to vice honored ceremonial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 懷遵子上賢，娶鎮王女崇安縣主。

translations.literal: Huaizun's son Shangxian married the Princess of Chong'an County, daughter of the Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizun's son Shangxian married the Princess of Chong'an, daughter of the Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 懷清子從湜，娶岐王女永壽縣主，為西京左藏庫副使，後坐事除名。

translations.literal: Huaqing's son Congshi married the Princess of Yongshou County, daughter of the Prince of Qi; he was Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury and later was struck from the rolls for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Huaqing's son Congshi married the Princess of Yongshou, daughter of the Prince of Qi; he served as vice commissioner of the western-capital left treasury and was later struck from the rolls for an offense.

sentences.zh: 張廷翰

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan

sentences.zh: 張廷翰，澤州陵川人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan was a man of Lingchuan in Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan was a native of Lingchuan in Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 初為漢祖親校。

translations.literal: He first served as a personal guard of the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a personal guard of the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，補內殿直，遷東西班軍使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered Bian he was appointed Inner Palace Direct Attendant and promoted to Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Class Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder entered Bian he was appointed an inner-palace direct attendant and promoted to commissioner of the eastern and western class armies.

sentences.zh: 周初，改護聖指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was changed to Commander of the Guard of Sacred Protection.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhou he was made commander of the Guard of Sacred Protection.

sentences.zh: 從世宗平淮甸，以功遷鐵騎右第二軍都虞候。
