translations.literal: He followed Shizong in pacifying the Huai region and for merit was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Right Second Army of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong in pacifying the Huai region and was promoted to deputy commander of the right second army of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 顯德末，改殿前散都頭都虞候。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiande he was changed to Deputy Commander of the Loose Chiefs before the Throne Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiande he was made deputy commander of the loose chiefs before the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 宋初，權為鐵騎左第二軍都校、領開州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was acting Colonel of the Left Second Army of the Iron Cavalry and given charge of Kaizhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was acting colonel of the left second army of the Iron Cavalry and prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 從平揚州，又以功遷控鶴左廂都指揮使、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of Yangzhou and again for merit was promoted to Commander of the Left Wing of the Crane Control Army and given charge as Regimental Commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Yangzhou and was promoted to commander of the left wing of the Crane Control Army and regimental commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉龍捷左廂都指揮使、領春州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Commander of the Left Wing of the Dragon Swift Army and given charge as Regimental Commissioner of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to commander of the left wing of the Dragon Swift Army and regimental commissioner of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，興師伐蜀，以廷翰為歸州路行營馬軍都指揮使，隨劉廷讓由歸州路進討。

translations.literal: During Qiande an army was raised against Shu; Tinghan was made Overall Commander of Cavalry on the Guizhou Route Campaign Headquarters and followed Liu Tingrang in advancing by the Guizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, on the Shu campaign, Tinghan was made overall commander of cavalry on the Guizhou route headquarters and advanced with Liu Tingrang along the Guizhou route.

sentences.zh: 師次夔州，廷讓頓兵白帝廟西，俄而夔州監軍武守謙率所部來拒戰，廷翰引兵逆擊，敗之於豬頭鋪，乘勝拔其城。

translations.literal: The army halted at Kuizhou; Tingrang encamped west of the White Emperor Shrine. Soon Wu Shouqian, military supervisor of Kuizhou, led his troops to resist; Tinghan led troops to meet the attack, defeated them at Zhutou Post, and taking advantage of the victory stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Kuizhou; Tingrang encamped west of the White Emperor Shrine. When Wu Shouqian, military supervisor of Kuizhou, came out to fight, Tinghan met him in battle, routed him at Zhutou Post, and stormed the city in the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，授侍衛馬步軍都虞候、領彰國軍節度。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was given the post of Overall Deputy of the Palace Horse and Foot Forces and charge as military governor of the Zhangguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was made overall deputy of the palace horse and foot forces and military governor of the Zhangguo Army.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，寢疾，太祖親臨問，未幾卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he fell gravely ill; Taizu personally came to inquire after him; soon he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he fell gravely ill; Taizu visited him in person; he died soon afterward at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明，冀州蓨人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming was a man of Tiao in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming was a native of Tiao in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父濟，汾川令。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Magistrate of Fenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was magistrate of Fenchuan.

sentences.zh: 繼明身長七尺，善騎射，以膂力聞郡中。

translations.literal: Jiming was seven feet tall, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and famed in the commandery for his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming stood seven feet tall, excelled at horsemanship and archery, and was famed throughout the commandery for his strength.

sentences.zh: 刺史張廷翰以隸左右，薦於太祖，補殿前指揮使，歷左右番押班都知。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Tinghan took him into his personal staff, recommended him to Taizu, and he was appointed Commander before the Throne Hall, serving successively as Chief of the Left and Right Palace Escort Classes.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Tinghan took him into his staff, recommended him to Taizu, and he was appointed a commander before the throne hall, rising through the left and right palace escort classes.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，改領洋州觀察使，充環慶路馬步軍都部署，繼明謹愿，御下嚴肅，士卒頗畏憚之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was changed to Military Commissioner of Yangzhou and made Overall Deployer of Horse and Foot Forces on the Huanqing Circuit; Jiming was careful and sincere, stern in commanding subordinates, and the troops greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao he was made military commissioner of Yangzhou and overall deployer of horse and foot forces on the Huanqing circuit; Jiming was careful and sincere, stern with his men, and the troops feared him.

sentences.zh: 二年，受詔護送輜重赴靈州，繼明已先約靈州部署田紹斌率軍迎援，適被病，裨將白守榮謂繼明曰：「君疾甚，不可行，恐失期會，守榮當率兵先往。

translations.literal: In the second year he received orders to escort baggage trains to Lingzhou; Jiming had already arranged for Tian Shaobin, deployer at Lingzhou, to lead troops to meet and support him. He happened to fall ill, and Vice General Bai Shourong said to Jiming, "Your illness is severe; you cannot travel, lest we miss the rendezvous — Shourong will lead the troops ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was ordered to escort supply trains to Lingzhou; Jiming had already arranged for Tian Shaobin at Lingzhou to meet him with reinforcements. When he fell ill, Vice General Bai Shourong said, "Your illness is too severe to travel — we may miss the rendezvous. Let me lead the troops ahead.

sentences.zh: 」繼明宿將，慮守榮等輕佻，與戎人接戰，因謂之曰：「我疾少間。

translations.literal: " Jiming was a veteran general and feared that Shourong and the others were frivolous in fighting the barbarians, so he said to them, "My illness will ease a little.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming was a veteran and feared Shourong's men were too rash against the enemy, so he said, "My illness will ease shortly.

sentences.zh: 」遂矍鑠被甲上馬，強行至清遠軍，卒，年六十三，詔贈彰武軍節度。

translations.literal: " He then roused himself, donned armor, mounted his horse, and forced his way to Qingyuan Army, where he died, aged sixty-three; an edict posthumously gave him the title of military governor of the Zhangwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He roused himself, donned armor, mounted, and forced his way to Qingyuan Army, where he died at sixty-three; the court posthumously granted him the title of military governor of the Zhangwu Army.

sentences.zh: 遷其子懷信為供奉官。

translations.literal: His son Huaixin was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaixin was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 張瓊，大名館陶人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiong was a man of Guantao in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiong was a native of Guantao in Daming.

sentences.zh: 世為牙中軍。

translations.literal: For generations his family served in the headquarters guard.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served for generations in the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 瓊少有勇力，善射，隸太祖帳下。

translations.literal: Qiong in youth had courage and strength, was skilled in archery, and served under Taizu's banner.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Qiong was strong and brave, skilled in archery, and entered Taizu's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，太祖從世宗南征，擊十八里灘砦，為戰艦所圍，一人甲盾鼓噪而前，眾莫敢當，太祖命瓊射之，一發而踣，淮人遂卻。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou, when Taizu followed Shizong on the southern campaign and attacked the stockade at Shibalitan, they were surrounded by warships; one man in armor and shield came forward shouting, and none dared meet him; Taizu ordered Qiong to shoot him — one shot and he fell; the Huai men then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhou Xiande, when Taizu followed Shizong south and attacked the stockade at Shibalitan, they were surrounded by warships; one armored man came forward shouting, and none dared face him; Taizu ordered Qiong to shoot — one arrow and the man fell, and the Huai forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 瓊性暴無機，多所淩轢。

translations.literal: Qiong was violent by nature and tactless, and often bullied others.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was violent and tactless by nature and often bullied others.

sentences.zh: 時史珪、石漢卿方用事，瓊輕侮之，目為巫媼。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Gui and Shi Hanqing were in power; Qiong treated them lightly and called them witch crones.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Gui and Shi Hanqing were in power, Qiong despised them and called them witch crones.

sentences.zh: 二人銜之切齒，發瓊擅乘官馬，納李筠隸僕，畜部曲百餘人，恣作威福，禁軍皆懼；

translations.literal: The two bore him bitter hatred and exposed that Qiong had usurped official horses, taken Li Yun's household servants, kept more than a hundred retainers, and acted arbitrarily with power and favor so that the palace troops all feared him;
translations.idiomatic: The two hated him bitterly and accused him of riding official horses without permission, taking Li Yun's household servants, keeping more than a hundred retainers, and abusing his power until the palace troops all feared him;

sentences.zh: 又誣毀太宗為殿前都虞候時事。

translations.literal: they also slandered affairs from when Taizong was Overall Deputy before the Throne Hall.
translations.idiomatic: they also slandered Taizong's conduct when he was deputy commander before the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年秋，郊禋制下，方欲肅靜京師，乃召訊瓊。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year of Jianlong, when the suburban sacrifice regulations were issued and the capital was to be quieted, Qiong was summoned for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year of Jianlong, as suburban sacrifice regulations were issued and the court sought to quiet the capital, Qiong was summoned for questioning.

sentences.zh: 瓊不伏，太祖怒，令擊之。

translations.literal: Qiong would not submit; Taizu was angry and ordered him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong would not confess; Taizu was furious and ordered him beaten.

sentences.zh: 漢卿即奮鐵撾亂下，氣垂絕，曳出，遂下御史案鞫之。

translations.literal: Hanqing immediately struck wildly with an iron club; Qiong was nearly dead and was dragged out; the case was then sent to the censorate for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing immediately beat him wildly with an iron club until he was nearly dead; he was dragged out and the case was sent to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 瓊知不免，行至明德門，解所係繫帶以遺母。

translations.literal: Qiong knew he could not escape; reaching the Gate of Bright Virtue he untied his belt and gave it to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Qiong at the Gate of Bright Virtue untied his belt and gave it to his mother.

sentences.zh: 獄具，賜死於城西井亭。

translations.literal: When the case was complete he was granted death at the well pavilion west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was proved he was granted death at the well pavilion west of the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖旋聞家無餘財，止有僕三人，甚悔之。

translations.literal: Taizu soon heard that the household had no surplus wealth and only three servants, and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu soon learned that the household had no wealth left and only three servants, and deeply regretted the affair.

sentences.zh: 因責漢卿曰：「汝言瓊有僕百人，今何在？

translations.literal: He therefore rebuked Hanqing, saying, "You said Qiong had a hundred servants — where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Hanqing: "You said Qiong had a hundred servants — where are they now?

sentences.zh: 」漢卿曰：「瓊所養者一敵百耳。

translations.literal: " Hanqing said, "Those Qiong kept were each a match for a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing answered, "The men Qiong kept were each a match for a hundred."

sentences.zh: 」太祖遂優恤其家。

translations.literal: " Taizu then treated his family with generous care.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then treated his family with generous care.

sentences.zh: 以其子尚幼，乃擢其兄進為龍捷副指揮使。

translations.literal: Because his son was still young, his elder brother Jin was promoted to Vice Commander of the Dragon Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son was still young, his elder brother Jin was promoted to vice commander of the Dragon Swift Army.

sentences.zh: 論曰：崔彥進與王全斌征蜀，黷貨殺降，以致蜀亂，惟劉廷讓一軍秋毫無犯，紀律嚴否於斯別矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Cui Yanjin and Wang Quanbin campaigned in Shu, took bribes and killed those who surrendered, bringing on the Shu turmoil — only Liu Tingrang's army took not so much as a hair; whether discipline was strict or lax is shown by this contrast.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: Cui Yanjin and Wang Quanbin on the Shu campaign took bribes and killed surrendering men, bringing on the Shu revolt — only Liu Tingrang's army took nothing at all; strict and lax discipline are plainly distinguished here.

sentences.zh: 尹崇珂斤斤謹厚，臨淄攻守之績，嶺嶠廓清之勞，至於瘁事。

translations.literal: Yin Chongke was scrupulous and steady; his achievements in attack and defense at Linzi and his labor in clearing the Ling ranges extended to the point of exhausting himself in service.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chongke was scrupulous and steady; his record at Linzi and his labor in pacifying Lingnan wore him out in the end.

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼明力疾以護軍行，純誠勇節，皆足嘉尚。

translations.literal: Huangfu Jiming forced himself on despite illness to escort the army march; his pure loyalty and brave integrity are all worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jiming forced himself onward despite illness to escort the army; his pure loyalty and courage are all worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 張廷翰西征，未睹奇效。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinghan on the western expedition showed no striking achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghan on the western expedition achieved nothing striking.

sentences.zh: 張美雖稱幹敏，而初有自愧之行。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, though praised for competence and alertness, had early conduct of which he himself was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, though praised for competence, had early conduct that left him ashamed.

sentences.zh: 郭守文敦詩閱禮，輕財好施，慎保封疆，士卒樂用，終以勳舊蒙眷，聯姻戚里。

translations.literal: Guo Shuowen was devoted to poetry and ritual, light with wealth and fond of giving, careful in guarding the frontier, and his troops were glad to serve; in the end, as an old merit-holder, he won favor and marriage ties with the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shuowen loved learning and ritual, was generous with wealth, guarded the frontier carefully, and won the loyalty of his troops; in the end, as an old merit-holder, he won imperial favor and marriage ties with the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 宋初諸將，要終而論，臧否異趣，何昭昭若是哉！

translations.literal: The generals of early Song — taking them all together in final judgment — show praise and blame in different directions; how clear and evident this is!
translations.idiomatic: The generals of early Song, judged in sum, show praise and blame running in different directions — how plainly this stands forth!
